ludwig-merckle.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
ludwig-merckle.summary: The reviewed sources describe Ludwig Merckle as sole heir to the Merckle group after the 2009 death of Adolf Merckle, with a corporate rescue negotiated with private creditor banks. They do not show political leverage, preferential state benefit or a wealth-to-power feedback loop.

support.text: dpa report: Ludwig Merckle to become sole heir of the Ulm group, whose estate includes stakes in HeidelbergCement, ratiopharm and Phoenix; banks required the ratiopharm sale as a bridge-loan condition.

counter.text: The same report mentions only a rescue negotiated with private creditor banks; it describes no government guarantee, political action or state benefit.

ludwig-merckle.limitations: Searches for political activity or lobbying by Ludwig Merckle found only business-press material on the 2009 crisis and succession; the Heidelberg Materials CV PDF could not be retrieved (404). Inheritance and shareholding alone do not justify points. This is a narrow review, not an exoneration: it reflects only the sources listed and may have missed lobbying, donation, contract or regulatory records. No numerical estimate is made.

sarath-ratanavadi.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
sarath-ratanavadi.period: Family background; 2020 LNG licensing; 2024 USC donor-influence reporting (unrelated to state power)
sarath-ratanavadi.summary: Reviewed sources record family ties to the military and an early-regulation-era energy business. Reporting on LNG import licences notes a licence to Gulf alongside reported state-utility reversals, but the author questions whether Gulf can translate wealth into market power. No source reviewed establishes personal leverage, preferential benefit and exchange together.
sarath-ratanavadi.mechanism: Possible access to energy licensing; not established

support.text: Father reported as former Thai armed-forces chief of staff; received a royal order in 2021. The page describes no government concession, contract or political role.
support.access: Page text reviewed; cited Nikkei and LA Times articles not opened

support.text: Government granted Gulf an LNG import licence (1.7 mtpa) in 2020; the author describes PTT, not Gulf, as the dominant political and market power.

counter.text: The Asia Times author calls Gulf's ability to turn wealth into market power an open question and says its LNG plans may never materialize.
The Wikipedia page gives no response from Ratanavadi on the USC admissions matter and reports no outcome; that matter concerns university admissions, not state power.

sarath-ratanavadi.limitations: Family military ties, a royal honour and a licence in a liberalizing sector do not by themselves show political leverage or preferential treatment. Thai-language and procurement/regulatory records were not reviewed. This is a narrow review, not an exoneration: it reflects only the sources listed and may have missed lobbying, donation, contract or regulatory records. No numerical estimate is made.

patrick-collison.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
patrick-collison.summary: Patrick Collison co-controls Stripe, joined Meta's board in 2025 and reportedly donated $7 million in 2026 to oppose a California billionaire wealth-tax measure. These show political expression and policy engagement, but the reviewed sources do not establish preferential benefit or an exchange.

support.text: Per the page: 2018 Stripe $1 million to California YIMBY (attributed to both brothers); $7 million in 2026 to a group opposing Proposition 40, a California billionaire wealth-tax proposal (citing the Irish Times, 29 July 2026); joined the Meta board in April 2025.
support.access: Page text reviewed; Irish Times and Irish Independent items not opened

counter.text: The page reports no lobbying activity or government contracts. Opposing a tax by donation is lawful political expression, and no outcome or benefit is documented. A web search tying Stripe to stablecoin lobbying returned nothing about the Collisons.

patrick-collison.limitations: The 2026 donation was not verified from the original report. Stripe's regulatory dealings and the Rhine Group role (uncited on the page) were not examined. This is a narrow review, not an exoneration: it reflects only the sources listed and may have missed lobbying, donation, contract or regulatory records. No numerical estimate is made.
